title: The performance difference lemma, softmax PG rates, and NPG
brief: Verify the identity behind every policy improvement result, measure the surrogate's second-order error, watch softmax policy gradient crawl at 1/t, and show that the natural gradient is a multiplicative-weights step.
hints: advantage is q_from_v(mdp, v) - v[:, None], with v from rlenvs.policy_evaluation(mdp, pi).

performance_difference and surrogate_gain differ in one argument: the lemma uses state_distribution(mdp, pi_new), the surrogate uses state_distribution(mdp, pi_old). Both divide by 1 - gamma, because state_distribution is normalised to sum to one.
In softmax_pg_bandit, record the policy before each update, so row 0 is the starting policy. Copy theta first, or you change the caller's array.
npg_step needs no Fisher matrix: multiply pi by exp(eta * A / (1 - gamma)) row by row, then renormalise. Subtract the row maximum of the exponent first, so eta = 10^4 doesn't overflow.
